text: What did the voice say? The voice said to the effect of you should kill the kids, this is your last chance so that you can kill yourself. And what did she say happened after she heard this voice? She engaged in the activity of taking her children's lives. After Lindsay Clancy killed all three of her children, she described something none of the doctors treating her beforehand had heard. She said a male voice told her she had no choice. She had to kill the children and then kill herself. So was this the missing evidence that she had really been psychotic or was it an explanation that appeared only after the killings? One of the first forensic experts to evaluate Lindsay after the children were killed was psychologist Dr. Paul Zeisel, brought in by her defense. Zeisel said Lindsay told Patrick during a phone call he witnessed that she had heard a male voice ordering her to kill the children and herself. He also tested whether Lindsay was faking or exaggerating symptoms and said he found no evidence that she was. Zeisel ultimately concluded that she was not criminally responsible. Then there was Dr. Philip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist and expert on parents who kill their children. He evaluated Lindsay about four months later and testified that she had been clearly psychotic. Resnick said Lindsay described feeling as if an outside force had taken control of her body, almost like she was a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings. According to him, Lindsay believed that if she killed herself, her children would suffer without her. In her delusional state, she believed they needed to die with her and go to heaven. But there's an obvious problem. None of the doctors treating Lindsay before the killings documented this male voice. Her psychiatrist didn't know about it, McLean didn't know about it, and Patrick didn't hear about it beforehand either. He testified that Lindsay first told him about the voice a week after the children's death. So if this voice was powerful enough to make her kill three children, why wasn't she telling anyone beforehand? The defense says psychotic patients can hide symptoms, especially if they're afraid their children could be taken away. The defense also calls this postpartum psychosis. But postpartum psychosis usually begins within days or weeks after childbirth and Callan was already eight months old, so the timing is unusual. The defense argues that her bipolar illness began postpartum and eventually developed into psychosis. But then we have the prosecution's expert. Forensic psychiatrist Dr. Avram Mack evaluated Lindsay in April 2026 and reached almost the opposite conclusion. He agreed she was suffering from severe major depression but said he found no evidence that she had been psychotic or manic and believed she could still understand right from wrong and control her actions. So we are looking at experts examining the same woman and reaching opposite conclusions. But these experts were not randomly assigned. Zizel and Resnick were brought in by the defense before they evaluated Lindsay. Mack was brought in by the prosecution before he evaluated her. That doesn't mean any of them are lying, but they knew which side had hired them. And each side naturally presents experts whose conclusions support its case. Which is why I think the doctors who actually treated Lindsay before the killings are especially important. They were treating her before there was a murder case and non-diagnosed psychosis. At the same time, that doesn't prove she wasn't psychotic. People can conceal psychotic symptoms and still perform normal organized tasks while experiencing delusions. So this is ultimately what the jury has to decide. Was Lindsay severely depressed but still understood what she was doing or was she genuinely psychotic? Hearing a male voice, believing an outside force was controlling her like a puppet, and thinking killing her children was somehow protecting them. One leads to murder, the other could mean she's found not criminally responsible. And this is where the case gets even messier outside the courtroom. Because a lot of people online have already picked a side and some are even blaming Patrick.
